claims.supported_wording: At the 2,221 allele sites retained in both PUF10 and PUF12, PUF12 showed a higher reported rate at 73.1% of sites, with a median within-site increase of 3.02 percentage points.
scope: Pairs are genomic allele keys chromosome/position/REF/ALT, not matched biological sample numbers.
Each rate is the existing four-source-replicate median. Site count is not biological replicate count.
The median is taken after subtracting the two rates within each site; it is not the difference of two marginal medians.
The result is conditional on retention in both frozen positive lists; absent sites receive no zero imputation.
Spearman is supplied descriptive correlation without a p-value or uncertainty interval.
Repeat extension was not isolated causally; expression, coverage and selection remain possible contributors.
required_cross_references: Connect to original Module 1 count result, then add same-site comparison.
unsupported_wording: Extension raises rates as a causal conclusion.
Editing specificity increased or safety improved merely because jointly retained rates increased.

claims.supported_wording: Lower retained-site counts can accompany weaker reported rates on shared sites: all 195 sites jointly retained by 132D and PUF12 had lower 132D rates, with a median difference of −18.86 percentage points. Candidate counts alone therefore do not certify specificity.
scope: Left panel is original Module 1 retained count divided by 12,908; right panel is a per-site difference median within each separate editor/PUF12 intersection.
Each editor comparison uses a different PUF12 subset; these differences do not rank variants on a common assessed site set.
E72A has an empty selected set, not a demonstrated zero editing rate.
Weaker shared-site signals are compatible with activity attenuation but do not isolate its molecular cause.
The two figure panels are not an efficiency-normalized specificity score.
required_cross_references: Say counts as in Module 1, re-normalized to PUF12; original data/captions remain intact.
unsupported_wording: Fewer candidate sites certify cleaner editing.
132D shows exactly zero editing elsewhere or every transcriptome site is attenuated.

claims.preferred_placement: Module 4 conclusion; recognition-mechanism boundary can be linked from Module 2 conclusion
claims.supported_wording: GCA remained the most common central triplet in all three selected-positive sets. The largest observed flanking-composition contrast was −6 G (PUF12-only minus PUF10-only, −19.78 percentage points), an exploratory feature from the complete position/base scan.
scope: Exclusive membership means selected in only one positive list, not zero editing in the other editor.
Set denominators are 553, 2,221 and 10,687 selected sites; each site has equal weight.
The neighbor panel shows marginal −1/+1 composition; the accompanying joint 16-triplet table supplies GCA proportions.
The flank figure shows all 404 position/base differences for PUF12-only minus PUF10-only. The CSV has 1,212 rows because two other full pairwise set contrasts are also retained.
The observed maximum is post hoc and descriptive; no p-value, background-enrichment test or equivalence test is supplied.
Same most-common triplet does not demonstrate identical core motifs, statistical equivalence, PUF-binding half sites, repeat-extension recruitment or dual-domain causality.
Raw positive-site sequences required to independently reproduce composition and assess half-site hypotheses are not included in this integration ZIP.
required_cross_references: State that original Module 1 per-editor logos and exclusive-set composition are complementary cuts of retained sites.
Keep exclusive-set composition figures away from the original motif-logo figure; their scopes differ.
unsupported_wording: PUF12-exclusive sites did not carry a different core motif.
The largest flanking difference is a newly recruited PUF half site or established binding motif.
Similar GCA percentages establish motif equivalence.

claims.preferred_placement: Module 3 conclusion; text and formula footnote only
claims.supported_wording: Within the archived combination-batch summaries, the triple mutant reduced C871 reporter signal by 57.3% and C388 reporter signal by 22.8%, increasing their ratio of means from 1.192 to 2.156.
claims.formula_footnote: The reported ratio 2.156 is mean(C388)/mean(C871); the retention index 0.773 is mean(C388) divided by the historical fixed reference 0.673. Using the observed parental mean 0.67335 yields 0.772; the separate mean-of-record-ratios calculation gives 2.157 and is not substituted for 2.156.
scope: The package supplies means/descriptive results from rounded archived source records, not the four underlying reporter sample rows or their original workbook.
Two source records per construct are not verified independent biological replicates; no confidence intervals or significance inference are justified.
Reporter signals are not background-subtracted net editing activity or isolated transgene conversion.
C871 is the measured reporter comparison endpoint; naming its relative reduction as a catalytic +1 preference change would overstate attribution.
The published 0.773 index preserves its historical fixed reference; it is not silently redefined using the observed parental mean.
Original/source references describe three batches with two triple records each; this package does not supply the six raw rows to verify their preservation independently.
The result does not establish final-construct transcriptome-wide specificity, toxicity reduction or therapeutic efficacy.
required_cross_references: Anchor to existing Module 3 assay figures; the package excludes the raw-record APOBEC figure.
unsupported_wording: The triple mutant improved net C388 activity.
The +1 catalytic endpoint was cut more than twice as deeply as on-target activity as a proven mechanism.
All 6 cross-batch raw records were independently verified by this integration audit.

scope: Matched-site counts per editor equal supplied summary shared counts.
